_comment: Phase 0 action palette. Matches docs/03-core-mechanics/action-palette.md. Times are in game-days. Costs are not enforced yet. §C4 — report_sender is a role_id token resolved through OrgRoles at fire time.

actions.blurb: Have your coordinator walk past the target's door, read the visitors, and write it down. No silver reaches the target; only coin reaches the coordinator's shoes. Weeks of waiting; almost no trace.
Invest quietly in a minor figure over many months, building the foundation of a future relationship. Your coordinator arranges the introductions and carries the gifts.
Introduce a concept into the target's thinking through a trusted intermediary. Slow burn.
Pay a trader on your coordinator's retainer to repeat something at the right wineshops until it sounds like common knowledge. No operatives needed yet; one patient voice is enough.
Use your shadow network to identify whoever is sharpening a blade for the throne, and buy, flatter, or frighten them back into line. Silver burns fast; traces stay faint.
Pay emissaries and pamphleteers to inflame the target kingdom's worst frontier. The aim is not a war today — it is to make tomorrow's war feel, to those involved, like their own idea.
A single, direct payment for a single, concrete act. Fast and cheap to arrange. A greedy or straitened hand takes it gladly; a proud one takes offence, loudly.
Pay them every month so the payments themselves become the loyalty. Once fed, they are easy to keep — and catastrophic if the meals ever stop. You take on a dependent.
No silver changes hands. An introduction at a better court, a patronage they could not win alone, a rival's fall arranged as though by the stars. Ambition is a hungrier buyer than greed.

Give them something they want — a rival's secret, an advance warning, a thread they can pull. They act for you; you and they now hold knives to each other's throats. A quiet arrangement, for the right kind of target.
A cask of wine at a name-day. A dowry covered through a 'distant cousin'. A business debt quietly forgiven. Nothing that could be called a bribe, if anyone asked. Slow; almost invisible.

actions.display_name: Have a host sway the court
actions.blurb: Through a loyal host, shape the next decision of the crown they serve. Their hand, not yours — exposure stays low.
Ask a loyal host to light popular anger in their own city. The throat shouting is theirs; the fingers holding the taper are yours.

Bring a trusted host fully into your work. They stop being an instrument and start being a hand of their own — running a cell in their city, picking their own operatives, answering only to you. A very dangerous conversation to have; once spoken, it cannot be taken back.

Raise a seasoned coordinator to the second-highest rank in your organisation. They will know the shape of what you are, though not what you are. Years of seasoning inside the cell are the only test that matters — do not rush it.

Have your coordinator sit with everything one source has sent in and compare it, line by line, against every other thread on the same ground. Fast, quiet, and tells you less than you would like — but the contradictions it finds are almost never wrong.

Put the operative themselves under the glass — their contacts, their lifestyle, the gap between what they say they spend and what they clearly do. If they are clean, you will only cost them sleep. If they are turned, they will know within weeks that they are watched.

Send your coordinator over the same ground a second time, without telling the original source. Slow and expensive, but the only method that tells you what is actually true, not merely what your existing thread agrees on.

Look inside one of your own cells. Compare the ledgers your coordinator keeps with what your financial network actually moved; walk the same ground their operatives report on. Long tenures with no audit are the tenures that rot.

Quietly move every operative under this coordinator to new duties, new faces, and new corners of the kingdom. Expensive, slow, and loud only to ourselves. Resets the heat around the cell; does not repair the trust lost with anyone we have already burned.

Send trusted auditors through the books of this institution. Every drawer. Every receipt. The director will know they were there. The drift will be pulled back; the message they send downstream will last a year.

A compromised source is not a problem — it is a chair at the other table. Turn them. Control what they carry upward. Bleeds your bandwidth every month and ends, eventually, in fire. Worth it, if the fire burns in the right direction.

Walk the ground under the last strange thing that happened in this region. Granary fires without a drought, decrees without an obvious author, succession that arranged itself. One pass of honest feet, asking questions that have to be paid for.

Take the pile of anomalies we have already broken open in this region and ask a harder question: is there a single hidden hand behind them? Slow, expensive, and only useful if we have done the groundwork.
Take a confirmed pattern and hold it up against the library of every rival signature we have catalogued. If the match is real, we will know the name of the hand that has been moving here.

Have your coordinator spend a season at the wrong tables — watching wrong gates, tracing unusual payments, sitting where locals do not. Sooner or later a face that does not belong to this region will show itself twice.

We have a name now. Take it off the board — burn them publicly, hand them to the crown, make sure the next one sent here knows what this city does to them. Loud, expensive, unambiguous. Your coordinator runs point until you have hands to delegate this to.

Do not burn them. Own them. A rival's ear in our city is worth more than a rival's corpse in it. Every month their handler hears what we decide they should hear — and every month we hear, cleanly, what their side is asking about.

When a region begins to talk about us — even without knowing we are the us they are talking about — we pay priests to preach other miracles, pamphleteers to print other conspiracies, drinkers to tell other stories. Patient work. Not heroic. Necessary.

A hunter believes. Belief cannot be bought or frightened. It can, sometimes, be made to look ridiculous. Salt their sources. Give them one wrong fact they will defend publicly. Let their colleagues do the rest. Fails loudly when it fails.

A historian is not a hunter in the street; they are a ledger in a room. The ledger is the threat. Burn the room. Scatter the chroniclers. Louder than we usually are, and costlier in stories told afterward — but historians cannot be silenced by discredit, only starved of what they read.

Do the work ourselves, but leave someone else's hand on it. A forged signature — the little tells a confirmed rival has taught us — costs them a region and buys us quiet. Fails loudly: a forgery spotted is a forgery catalogued, and the catalogue now points back at us.

We have catalogued a society deeply enough to know there is an immortal behind it. A discreet letter can be sent through intermediaries. They may answer. They may ignore us. They may take the letter as the provocation it, in some senses, is.

A truce between us and them. Their society stops acting against our regions; ours stops acting against theirs. Neither side can enforce it — but both understand what the alternative looks like, and both have lived long enough to prefer silence.

The most dangerous action in any campaign. If it works, their society goes posthumous and its tempo collapses. If it fails, a peer who now knows our shape is alive, angry, and has centuries of practice at what we do. Not to be ordered lightly.
